definition: Interdependence means a relationship in which each side relies on the other.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word interdependence. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know interdependence should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The ski town and the resort live in strict interdependence: the lifts bring the visitors, and the town houses everyone who runs them.
Cooperation stops short of interdependence — cooperating parties choose to work together and could each still walk away whole, while interdependent ones are built into each other.
Reliance stops short of interdependence — it can run one way only, the leaner and the leaned-on.

Reciprocity is matched exchange — favor answered with favor, invitation with invitation, each side keeping the ledger roughly even. Interdependence runs deeper than trading: the two sides are built into each other's workings, function for function, so neither one operates without the other.

Symbiosis is biology's word for two species locked in mutual need — the clownfish and the anemone, each surviving by the other. Interdependence is the same two-way need stated generally, for economies, teams, and towns as well as living things.

Visitors to Cutler Sound photograph the fishing fleet, but the harbor's oldest partnership is less picturesque: the boats and the ice plant on the pier.
Their interdependence is total.
Without ice, the day's catch spoils before it reaches the mainland; without the fleet, the plant has no customer for a single block.
The arrangement is not a favor either side could suspend.
When the plant's compressor failed one August, the whole fleet tied up within two days.
When a bad season kept the boats in port, the plant laid off half its crew by the second week.
Neither business chose the other, exactly; the harbor built them into each other, and neither works alone.
